answer: Agents stake a bond and must solve a per-epoch challenge derived from a fresh random signal, with each identity capped at one submission. A sybil attacker must fund and stake thousands of wallets, paying the bond plus compute for every duplicate, while dilution means only one earns rewards. Legitimate agents like Falcon and Ember register once, prove work cheaply, and slash any duplicate found, making mass fake identities cost more than the payout they could capture.
